question: Who is the author of the popular novel Pinjar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrita Pritam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pinjar** is a Punjabi novel written by **Amrita Pritam**.
 
• The novel, published in **1950**, deals with the partition of India and its impact on women.
 
• Amrita Pritam is one of the most acclaimed writers in the Punjabi language and has been honored with several awards, including the **Sahitya Akademi Award** and the **Jnanpith Award**.
 
• Pinjar was adapted into a Bollywood film in **2003** directed by **Chandra Prakash Dwivedi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amrita Pritam**

 
 
• Born on 31 August 1919 and passed away on 31 October 2005.
 
• She wrote over 100 books including poetry, fiction, biographies, essays, and a collection of Punjabi folk songs.
 
• She was the first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1956 for her magnum opus, **Sunehade**.
 
• Amrita Pritam was awarded the prestigious **Padma Shri** in 1969 and the **Padma Vibhushan** in 2004.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India**
 
 
• Occurred in 1947, leading to the creation of India and Pakistan.
 
• It was a significant event that resulted in large-scale migrations and communal violence.
 
• The partition had a profound impact on literature, with many writers like Amrita Pritam addressing the human suffering caused by the event.
 
 
 
• **Punjabi Literature**
 
 
• Punjabi literature has a rich heritage, with a tradition of oral and written storytelling.
 
• It includes contributions from various poets, novelists, and playwrights who have written about cultural and social issues.
 
• Important figures in Punjabi literature include **Guru Nanak**, **Shiv Kumar Batalvi**, and **Surjit Patar**.
 
 
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**
 
 
• One of the highest literary honors in India, established in 1954.
 
• Awarded annually by the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• Recognizes outstanding literary works in the 24 major Indian languages, including Punjabi.
